children: Axa raised its profitability and cash-generation targets for 2027 to 2029 on Tuesday, saying its diversified business would drive earnings growth despite softening market conditions at Axa XL.
The French insurer set out four main financial targets in the new three-year plan, including increased targets for earnings growth and return on equity.
Axa said it was targeting annual earnings per share growth of between 7% and 9%, compared with 2026 guidance of 6% to 8%.
Under its 2027 to 2029 plan, Axa is targeting an ROE of 15% to 17%, compared with 2026 guidance of 14% to 16%.
For both metrics, Axa said it expected to be at the top end of the target range in 2026.

The group also stated that it would generate around €25 billion ($28.8 billion) of cash remittances over the new plan period, while maintaining a 75% payout ratio, which would be prioritised over further M&A activity.

Axa said it expected continued softening conditions at Axa XL and would focus on disciplined underwriting rather than chasing growth for the division, which accounted for 17% of group revenue in 2025.

The insurer said it aimed to gain market share in retail P&C, small and medium-sized enterprises and mid-market insurance, and life and health over the next three years, which represented 83% of group revenue in 2025.

Axa said its solvency ratio remained strong, bolstered by reduced sensitivity to interest rate changes and stress scenarios. The group estimates the upcoming Solvency II reforms in Q1 2027 could add 17 percentage points to its solvency ratio.

"Our plan for 2027 to 2029 is one of disciplined growth and execution, with more ambitious targets for underlying EPS growth and RoE, and the introduction of a new book value per share growth target," said Alban de Mailly Nesle, chief financial officer of Axa.

Axa said it expected AI-driven initiatives and business improvements to generate €500 million to €700 million of recurring annual pre-tax benefits by 2029, through savings in pricing, underwriting, claims and operations.
Axa targets 7% to 9% annual EPS growth and 15% to 17% ROE for 2027 to 2029
Group targets around €25 billion of cash remittances while maintaining 75% payout ratio
Axa estimates Solvency II reforms in Q1 2027 could add 17 percentage points to solvency ratio
